# Input reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_docs.py from good/schema.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every component validates its inputs against these fields when it is added to a network.
Units are listed in [Units](units.md). Any other key (for example `fuel`, `jurisdiction` or
`co2`) is kept as a free-form attribute that policy filters can use.

## Region

Node class. One per balancing region.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `shortfall_capacity` | unset | Maximum unserved energy per step (MW). |
| `shortfall_cost` | unset | Cost of unserved energy ($/MWh). |
| `wastage_capacity` | unset | Maximum dumped surplus per step (MW). |
| `wastage_cost` | unset | Cost of dumping surplus energy ($/MWh). |

## Link

Edge class. Holds the transmission lines from its source region to its target.

No fields beyond free-form attributes.

## Producer

Asset class for generators, including wind, solar and hydro.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `capex_capacity` | `0.0` | Maximum new capacity the model may build (MW); inf for unlimited. |
| `capex_cost` | `0.0` | Overnight capital cost of new capacity ($/MW). |
| `fom_cost` | `0.0` | Fixed O&M cost of new capacity ($/MW-yr). |
| `lifetime` | unset | Economic lifetime used to annualize capex_cost (years). |
| `discount_rate` | unset | Real discount rate; defaults to the Network's discount_rate. |
| `capital_charge_rate` | unset | Annual charge per unit of overnight cost; overrides lifetime and discount_rate. |
| `installed_capacity` | `0.0` | Existing capacity (MW). |
| `operating_cost` | `0.0` | Variable cost of production ($/MWh). |
| `profile` | unset | Per-unit availability by time step. Omit for 1.0 in every step. |
| `capacity_factor` | `1.0` | Multiplies the profile; with no profile it is a flat availability. |
| `dispatchable` | `True` | False fixes output at availability (must-take or must-run). |
| `min_output` | `0.0` | Minimum output as a fraction of capacity in every step. |
| `ramp_rate` | unset | Maximum change in output per hour as a fraction of capacity. |
| `energy_budget_window` | unset | When set, the profile is an energy budget: output over each window of this many steps may not exceed the summed availability, and hourly output may reach full capacity. |
| `capacity_credit` | `1.0` | Fraction of capacity counted toward reserve margins. |

## Store

Asset class for storage.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `capex_capacity` | `0.0` | Maximum new capacity the model may build (MW); inf for unlimited. |
| `capex_cost` | `0.0` | Overnight capital cost of new capacity ($/MW). |
| `fom_cost` | `0.0` | Fixed O&M cost of new capacity ($/MW-yr). |
| `lifetime` | unset | Economic lifetime used to annualize capex_cost (years). |
| `discount_rate` | unset | Real discount rate; defaults to the Network's discount_rate. |
| `capital_charge_rate` | unset | Annual charge per unit of overnight cost; overrides lifetime and discount_rate. |
| `installed_capacity` | `0.0` | Existing charge/discharge power (MW). |
| `duration` | unset | Hours of storage at full power; sets energy capacity of existing and new builds. |
| `installed_energy` | unset | Existing energy capacity (MWh); overrides installed_capacity x duration. |
| `charge_efficiency` | `1.0` | One-way charging efficiency. |
| `discharge_efficiency` | `1.0` | One-way discharging efficiency. |
| `operating_cost` | `0.0` | Variable cost per MWh discharged ($/MWh). |
| `energy_capex_cost` | `0.0` | Overnight cost of new energy capacity ($/MWh), added to capex_cost. |
| `cyclic` | `True` | State of charge at the end of the horizon wraps to the start. |
| `initial_soc` | `0.0` | Starting state of charge as a fraction of energy capacity (cyclic=False only). |
| `capacity_credit` | `1.0` | Fraction of power capacity counted toward reserve margins. |

Removed in 2.0 (rejected with an explanation):

* `production_rate`: Use installed_capacity (MW) with duration (h) or installed_energy (MWh). See docs/migration.md, or convert v1 graphs with good.migrate.from_v1().
* `consumption_rate`: Use installed_capacity (MW) with duration (h) or installed_energy (MWh). See docs/migration.md, or convert v1 graphs with good.migrate.from_v1().
* `efficiency`: Use charge_efficiency and discharge_efficiency (one-way). See docs/migration.md, or convert v1 graphs with good.migrate.from_v1().
* `initial`: Stores are cyclic by default; set cyclic=False and initial_soc (fraction) instead. See docs/migration.md, or convert v1 graphs with good.migrate.from_v1().

## Load

Asset class for demand.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `installed_capacity` | `0.0` | Demand scale (MW); the profile multiplies it. |
| `profile` | unset | Per-unit demand by time step. Omit for constant demand. |
| `flex_capacity` | `0.0` | Maximum demand that can be deferred or made up in one step (MW). |
| `flex_max_delay` | unset | Deferred demand must be served within this many hours. |
| `flex_max_advance` | unset | Demand served early must be due within this many hours. |
| `flex_efficiency` | `1.0` | Energy served per unit deferred; below 1 means shifting costs energy. |
| `flex_cost` | `0.0` | Cost per MWh of deferred demand ($/MWh). |

Removed in 2.0 (rejected with an explanation):

* `shift_capacity`: Load shifting is now flexible demand: use flex_capacity (MW) and flex_max_delay (h). See docs/migration.md, or convert v1 graphs with good.migrate.from_v1().
* `shift_window`: Load shifting is now flexible demand: use flex_max_delay and flex_max_advance (h). See docs/migration.md, or convert v1 graphs with good.migrate.from_v1().
* `capex_capacity`: Loads are demand only and cannot be expanded; model generation as a Producer. See docs/migration.md, or convert v1 graphs with good.migrate.from_v1().
* `capex_cost`: Loads are demand only and cannot be expanded; model generation as a Producer. See docs/migration.md, or convert v1 graphs with good.migrate.from_v1().

## Transmission

Line class for directed transfer paths.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `capex_capacity` | `0.0` | Maximum new capacity the model may build (MW); inf for unlimited. |
| `capex_cost` | `0.0` | Overnight capital cost of new capacity ($/MW). |
| `fom_cost` | `0.0` | Fixed O&M cost of new capacity ($/MW-yr). |
| `lifetime` | unset | Economic lifetime used to annualize capex_cost (years). |
| `discount_rate` | unset | Real discount rate; defaults to the Network's discount_rate. |
| `capital_charge_rate` | unset | Annual charge per unit of overnight cost; overrides lifetime and discount_rate. |
| `installed_capacity` | `0.0` | Existing transfer capability (MW). |
| `efficiency` | `1.0` | Share of sent energy that arrives. |
| `operating_cost` | `0.0` | Wheeling cost per MWh sent ($/MWh). |
| `corridor` | unset | Lines with the same corridor share one expansion decision, so the two directions of a path are expanded and paid for once. |

## Portfolio_Standard

Policy: share of generation from included assets.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `non_compliance_capacity` | `0.0` | Largest allowed shortfall against the policy. |
| `non_compliance_cost` | `0.0` | Cost per unit of shortfall. |
| `ratio` | **required** | Required share of included generation. |
| `include` | `…` | Filter for qualifying assets. |
| `exclude` | unset | Filter for the other assets in the denominator. |

Removed in 2.0 (rejected with an explanation):

* `inclusion_criteria`: Use 'include' with an attribute filter. Convert v1 files with good.migrate.convert_policies().
* `exclusion_criteria`: Use 'exclude' with an attribute filter. Convert v1 files with good.migrate.convert_policies().

## Capacity_Target

Policy: minimum capacity of included assets.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `non_compliance_capacity` | `0.0` | Largest allowed shortfall against the policy. |
| `non_compliance_cost` | `0.0` | Cost per unit of shortfall. |
| `target` | **required** | Minimum capacity (MW). |
| `include` | `…` | Filter for qualifying assets. |

Removed in 2.0 (rejected with an explanation):

* `inclusion_criteria`: Use 'include' with an attribute filter. Convert v1 files with good.migrate.convert_policies().

## Reserve_Margin

Policy: credited capacity above peak demand.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `non_compliance_capacity` | `0.0` | Largest allowed shortfall against the policy. |
| `non_compliance_cost` | `0.0` | Cost per unit of shortfall. |
| `margin` | **required** | Required margin above demand (0.15 for 15%). |
| `demand` | `…` | Filter for loads. |
| `supply` | `…` | Filter for credited assets. |

Removed in 2.0 (rejected with an explanation):

* `sign`: Loads are positive since GOOD 2.0, so no sign flip is needed. See docs/migration.md, or convert v1 graphs with good.migrate.from_v1().
* `demand_criteria`: Use 'demand' with an attribute filter. Convert v1 files with good.migrate.convert_policies().
* `supply_criteria`: Use 'supply' with an attribute filter. Convert v1 files with good.migrate.convert_policies().
